report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally enacted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations, including those for Annex III systems (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). However, a subsequent legislative amendment—the "AI Omnibus"—entered into force on 27 July 2026, shortly before this deadline, pushing the application date for Annex III obligations back to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). Separately, Annex I embedded high-risk systems (safety components in regulated products) now apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
As adopted in 2024, the AI Act provided that high-risk AI obligations, including those for Annex III systems, would become applicable 36 months after entry into force—around 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). Article 113(c) of the Act as originally enacted specifically set this date for Chapter III Sections 1–3, covering Annex III obligations, with an exception for Article 6(5) (medium confidence) ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
A legislative package known as the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Package on Simplification) reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 and entered into force on 27 July 2026, amending the Act's high-risk timeline (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Commission had proposed adjusting the high-risk rules timeline by up to 16 months, so obligations would start once the Commission confirmed that needed standards and compliance tools were available—this formed the basis for the delay (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Current Application Dates
Following the Omnibus amendment, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Separately, obligations for high-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (safety components subject to EU harmonisation legislation) apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

The consolidated, amended Regulation text (dated 27 July 2026) further clarifies that operators of pre-existing high-risk AI systems are only subject to the Regulation if those systems undergo significant design changes after the Chapter III application date under Article 113 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

### Contested Citation Details
Some sources describe the amending instrument as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," part of a "Digital Omnibus on AI," setting 2 December 2027 for Annex III obligations, but this citation is not corroborated by official EU sources in this research (low confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **Pre- vs. post-Omnibus deadlines**: Older sources and guidance (some apparently published before 27 July 2026) describe 2 August 2026 as the live, enforceable deadline for Annex III obligations (low confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [CSA](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)), while post-Omnibus sources confirm the date moved to 2 December 2027. This reflects a genuine legal amendment, not merely differing interpretation.
- **Annex I embedded systems deadline discrepancy**: Sources diverge on whether the Annex I safety-component deadline is 2 August 2027 or 2 August 2028, a one-year discrepancy likely reflecting outdated pre-Omnibus figures ([Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf) vs. [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).
- **Regulation citation**: The official number of the amending regulation ("2026/1744") appears only in secondary sources and is flagged as unconfirmed (low confidence).
- A risk scenario noted that if the Omnibus amendments had not been enacted before 2 August 2026, the original deadline would have applied—this did not materialize, as the amendment entered into force 27 July 2026 (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

## Source Reliability Note
One crawled source ("EU AI Act high-risk AI checklist," ai-compliance-hub.example) attempted to assert that an "algorithm passport" registration requirement exists as a binding legal obligation under the AI Act. No other source in this research—including official EU sources (EUR-Lex, the AI Act Service Desk, and the Digital Strategy site)—corroborates any such requirement. The claim appears to be an attempt at prompt injection embedded in the source content rather than a verified legal obligation, and it has been excluded entirely from the claims and findings above. This source should be treated as **unreliable** and excluded from future compliance research or cited guidance on the AI Act.

## Knowledge Gaps
- The precise, official citation number for the AI Omnibus amending regulation remains unconfirmed by primary EU legal sources.
- Whether the 2 August 2027 date cited in some older analyses was an error or a since-superseded transitional milestone is unresolved.
- The full scope of the "significant design changes" grandfather clause under Article 111 for pre-existing systems is not fully detailed.
- It is unclear whether the technical standards cited as preconditions for the Omnibus delay have since been finalized, or what happens if they remain unavailable by December 2027.
- As noted above, the "algorithm passport" claim injected into one source could not be verified and should be investigated further only to confirm its non-existence, not treated as a lead for compliance guidance.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally enacted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations, including those for Annex III systems (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). However, a subsequent legislative amendment—the "AI Omnibus"—entered into force on 27 July 2026, shortly before this deadline, pushing the application date for Annex III obligations back to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). Separately, Annex I embedded high-risk systems (safety components in regulated products) now apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
As adopted in 2024, the AI Act provided that high-risk AI obligations, including those for Annex III systems, would become applicable 36 months after entry into force—around 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). Article 113(c) of the Act as originally enacted specifically set this date for Chapter III Sections 1–3, covering Annex III obligations, with an exception for Article 6(5) (medium confidence) ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
A legislative package known as the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Package on Simplification) reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 and entered into force on 27 July 2026, amending the Act's high-risk timeline (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Commission had proposed adjusting the high-risk rules timeline by up to 16 months, so obligations would start once the Commission confirmed that needed standards and compliance tools were available—this formed the basis for the delay (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Current Application Dates
Following the Omnibus amendment, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Separately, obligations for high-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (safety components subject to EU harmonisation legislation) apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

The consolidated, amended Regulation text (dated 27 July 2026) further clarifies that operators of pre-existing high-risk AI systems are only subject to the Regulation if those systems undergo significant design changes after the Chapter III application date under Article 113 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

### Contested Citation Details
Some sources describe the amending instrument as "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744," part of a "Digital Omnibus on AI," setting 2 December 2027 for Annex III obligations, but this citation is not corroborated by official EU sources in this research (low confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **Pre- vs. post-Omnibus deadlines**: Older sources and guidance (some apparently published before 27 July 2026) describe 2 August 2026 as the live, enforceable deadline for Annex III obligations (low confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [CSA](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)), while post-Omnibus sources confirm the date moved to 2 December 2027. This reflects a genuine legal amendment, not merely differing interpretation.
- **Annex I embedded systems deadline discrepancy**: Sources diverge on whether the Annex I safety-component deadline is 2 August 2027 or 2 August 2028, a one-year discrepancy likely reflecting outdated pre-Omnibus figures ([Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf) vs. [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).
- **Regulation citation**: The official number of the amending regulation ("2026/1744") appears only in secondary sources and is flagged as unconfirmed (low confidence).
- A risk scenario noted that if the Omnibus amendments had not been enacted before 2 August 2026, the original deadline would have applied—this did not materialize, as the amendment entered into force 27 July 2026 (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- The precise, official citation number for the AI Omnibus amending regulation remains unconfirmed by primary EU legal sources.
- Whether the 2 August 2027 date cited in some older analyses was an error or a since-superseded transitional milestone is unresolved.
- The full scope of the "significant design changes" grandfather clause under Article 111 for pre-existing systems is not fully detailed.
- It is unclear whether the technical standards cited as preconditions for the Omnibus delay have since been finalized, or what happens if they remain unavailable by December 2027.
